categories.title: Before writing
categories.blurb: Before there were temples there were burials, painted animals and seasons kept by counting moons. What survives is practice, and the names for it are later words.

categories.title: The ancient Near East
categories.blurb: The first cities wrote their gods down: temple accounts, hymns, law codes. These are the traditions that named a god, a house for it, and a calendar for feeding it.

categories.title: Greece and Rome
categories.blurb: A civic religion of sacrifice and festival, and beside it the schools that argued about what a good life is. The two were never as separate as the word religion suggests.

categories.title: The north and the steppe
categories.blurb: Gods kept in groves and rivers, a world explained by kinship and weather, and a sky god the steppe carried from the Danube to the Gobi.

categories.title: Africa, the Americas and the Pacific
categories.blurb: Traditions that kept no scripture and needed none: a lineage of the living, a landscape with owners, and a calendar read from the sky.

categories.title: The Dharmic traditions
categories.blurb: Traditions that put the question of the self first, and answer it with practice: a path, a discipline, a liberation. They share a vocabulary and argue inside it.

categories.title: The East Asian traditions
categories.blurb: Ancestors at the hearth, a way that cannot be named, and a state that needed both. Here a school of thought and a temple are often the same building.

categories.title: The Abrahamic faiths
categories.blurb: One god, one book, and a family argument that has lasted three thousand years. The branches here disagree about almost everything except where they came from.

categories.title: The diasporas and the living indigenous paths
categories.blurb: Carried across an ocean and rebuilt from what could be remembered: a drum, a name, a leaf. These are traditions that survived by changing.

categories.title: The esoteric paths
categories.blurb: A secret is a way of keeping a teaching small. These paths read the world as a cipher, and the reading itself as the practice.

categories.title: Modern paganism and the new movements
categories.blurb: The last two centuries invented religions as fast as they dissolved them: revivals of old gods, science turned into scripture, and a book written yesterday.
